lacuna.repo_anchor: plan/0005-format-interop/README.md Stages 8-9 - '8. MXFP4 adapter: E2M1 values via a 16-entry nibble LUT, E8M0 block scales as power-of-two FP16 multiplies (32-element blocks). 9. NVFP4 adapter: E2M1 nibble LUT + E4M3 block scales (16-element blocks); the scale conversion reuses the FP8 rebias' - under the plan thesis 'when a model ships in a format that upstream vLLM gates to sm_80+ silicon (FP8 today; MXFP4/NVFP4 and friends tomorrow), this hardware loads and runs it immediately... so incoming models are testable on Turing before llama.cpp backports the format'; the same README's strategy skeleton ('a new format is a checkpoint adapter plus a row in the strategy registry, not a new program'; emulate = headline with block/tile scales reusing 'the accumulator-domain scale machinery from plan/0004') and Stage 5 ('format axis in selection') are the wiring these two adapters ride; MEMORY.md 2026-09-07 records plan/0005 as an open audited milestone (open plans' READMEs stay audited for the task-receipt gate); sibling lacuna records already bank the shared substrate: w4a16-perf-acceptance.json ('Marlin for Turing' port mechanics and NVFP4A16-on-sm75 status), d512-chunked-mma.json and gdn-linear-attention-sm75.json (Triton 3.3 FMA floor, lane pin triton <=3.2), turing-engine-upstream-drift.json (the engine row that gates every other row).
lacuna.current_status: As of 2026-09-07 the FP4-quantized checkpoint ecosystem is large, NVIDIA/Neural-Magic-driven, and nominally Turing-inclusive for NVFP4 while explicitly Turing-exclusive for MXFP4 - and the one nominally-supported Turing path has a public correctness record of failure. Format facts (stable): MXFP4 is the OCP MX v1.0 format (spec final 2023-09; arXiv:2310.10537) - E2M1 elements (1s/2e/1m, values {0,0.5,1,1.5,2,3,4,6} x sign) with a shared E8M0 power-of-two scale per 32-element block; NVFP4 is NVIDIA's finer variant (developer.nvidia.com blog, 2025) - same E2M1 elements, E4M3 per-16-element block scales plus a per-tensor FP32 global scale (two-level scaling; double the scale storage of MXFP4, better accuracy). Both scale types are exactly representable in FP16 (E4M3 by the sign-shift + exponent-rebias the FP8 stage already uses; E8M0 as a power-of-two multiply), so the plan's lossless-dequant premise holds. v0.14.0 movement (tag 2026-01-16, notes 2026-01-20), all Neural Magic/Red Hat unless noted: #30598 (merged 2025-12-18) made Marlin the default MXFP4 LoRA backend (Triton default demoted after the 'garbage output' accuracy bug, issue #29539 FULL_AND_PIECEWISE cudagraph interaction; benchmarks gpt-oss-20b + GSM8K LoRA: Marlin 1910 vs Triton 1820 output tok/s); #30881 (merged 2026-01-08, dsikka) 'NVFP4 Marlin for NVFP4A16 MoEs' via a unified _is_nvfp4_format detector and select_nvfp4_moe_backend(), validated on SM100 and SM90 only; #31926 (merged 2026-01-10, mgoin) MXFP4 W4A16 dense (scheme CompressedTensorsW4A16Mxfp4, later folded into the w4a4_mxfp4 scheme family; activation quant dropped, weight-only Marlin; GSM8K 0.652 on nm-testing/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct-MXFP4); MoE follow-ups #32284/#32285 (2026-01-13); all under the #29901/#31000 'Marlin for Turing (sm75)' umbrella (merged 2025-12-16/19) which added GPTQ/AWQ/FP8/NVFP4 Marlin to sm75 but excluded MXFP4 ('needs BF16 activation, which Turing lacks'; the author's brief MXFP4xFP16 variant was reverted at mgoin's request). Current floors (vLLM main, code-verified 2026-09-07): mxfp4.py (gpt-oss path, triton_kernels) get_min_capability=80 and get_supported_act_dtypes=[bfloat16] only; compressed_tensors/schemes/compressed_tensors_w4a4_mxfp4.py min capability 80; compressed_tensors_w4a4_nvfp4.py (CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4, use_a16 flag = NVFP4A16) min capability 75 - i.e. NVFP4 is nominally CC>=75. The official quantization docs table marks Marlin (GPTQ/AWQ/FP8/FP4) Turing as supported-with-asterisk and states verbatim '*Turing does not support Marlin MXFP4'. Correctness record below the Blackwell line: #33461 (2026-01-31, iori2333) - Marlin NVFP4 GEMM on 2x RTX 2080 Ti with vLLM 0.15.0 emits garbage ('!!' loops) on Qwen3-14B-NVFP4 while the same setup on an RTX 5060 Ti is coherent; no maintainer diagnosis, closed stale 'not planned'; #34694 (2026-02-17, still open) - BF16 NVFP4 Marlin garbled on any GPU without native FP4 (RTX 4090 tested, V100 noted): dequant_fp8_scales<nv_bfloat162,kFE4M3fn> widens E4M3 scales to BF16 with zero- instead of sign-filled middle exponent bits, scales near 2^0 read as ~2^-112, weights underflow to zero (54.7% zeros, cosine 0.22 vs FP32); fixed by #34577 (merged 2026-03-17, power-of-two prescale so MSB=1 holds; validated GLM-4.7-Flash-NVFP4 GSM8K 81.3-81.7% on RTX 4090), re-landed as #37465 (2026-03-18, Nemotron-3-Super assertion removed) with follow-ups #37502 and #33972 (FP16 NaN/Inf) - the most plausible cause of #33461's garbage, unconfirmed because #33461 predates the fix and records no dtype [uncertain]; #35922 (2026-03-03, closed not planned) - on A100 (SM80) compressed-tensors Qwen3-30B-A3B: FP4 Marlin MoE modes (NVFP4A16/MXFP4A16/NVFP4) fail with cudaErrorNoKernelImageForDevice (FP4 MoE kernels not compiled for SM80) while dense FP4 works and W4A16-INT4 MoE crashes with cudaErrorIllegalAddress - evidence the Marlin FP4 MoE binary coverage below SM89 is incomplete [uncertain for sm75 specifically]; #38022 (2026-03-24, closed not planned) - Marlin MoE MXFP4 gpt-oss-20b (K=N=2880, not %128) crashes 'Invalid thread config' even on Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 (vLLM 0.18.0), workaround FP8 dynamic - an alignment surface the fork's dispatch must gate loudly. gpt-oss CC-floor thread #23203 (2025-08-19, closed not planned): asks mxfp4.py floor 80 -> 7.5, citing transformers v4.55.2 PR #39940 which already runs MXFP4 at CC 7.5; no maintainer response. Fallback semantics upstream: on non-CC>=9.0 GPUs vLLM 'will default to dequantizing the model' to BF16 (warning requires triton >= 3.4.0 + triton_kernels) - i.e. upstream's only pre-Ampere answer is 4x-memory BF16 dequant, which sm75 cannot even feed to tensor cores. Community: weicj/vLLM-2080Ti-Definitive (dual 2080 Ti, base v0.21.0) lists NVFP4 among its served Marlin routes (post-fix evidence, no published transcript) [uncertain]; llama.cpp shipped gpt-oss MXFP4 at launch 2025-08 (guide #15396: MXFP4 ~ Q4_0, dequant-at-runtime on all pre-Blackwell GPUs; native-MXFP4 kernels only in PR #17906 for Blackwell) - the 'before llama.cpp backports' framing is already expired for gpt-oss but not for NVFP4, which llama.cpp does not execute natively (checkpoints get re-quantized to GGUF quants, losing the stored-value contract).
lacuna.sm75_viability: What actually runs on Turing (T4/2080 Ti/RTX 6000) today: (1) NVFP4A16 dense via upstream Marlin is NOMINALLY available (min capability 75, code-verified) but has one public real-Turing report and it is a failure - #33461, garbage output on 2080 Ti, v0.15.0, closed without diagnosis; the BF16 scale-widening bug (#34694) plus its March 2026 fix chain (#34577/#37465/#37502/#33972) is the most likely but unverified explanation, so 'NVFP4A16-Marlin-on-Turing after 2026-03-18' must be treated as unproven until run [uncertain]; forcing --dtype float16 avoids the BF16 widening entirely (the FP16 exponent maps directly) and is the documented-adjacent workaround implied by #34694. (2) NVFP4A16 MoE via Marlin on sm75: no evidence it was ever compiled or validated - #30881 validated SM90/SM100 only, and #35922 shows the FP4 MoE kernels missing entirely on SM80 [uncertain for sm75]; nm-testing/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-NVFP4A16 is the reference MoE checkpoint. (3) MXFP4 in every upstream shape is closed to Turing: the gpt-oss path is BF16-activation-only (mxfp4.py), Marlin MXFP4 is sm80+ (#31926 scheme floor 80; #29901 explicitly excluded it; docs: 'Turing does not support Marlin MXFP4'). (4) The recast path (the plan's fallback) is fully viable on sm75 today via HF transformers (CC 7.5 support since transformers v4.55.2 PR #39940) - E2M1 x E8M0/E4M3 dequant to fp16 at load, exact, 4x memory - and is the only currently-working upstream-stack route to gpt-oss MXFP4 bits on this host that does not require BF16 execution. (5) The emulate path (headline) is the fork's own: nibble LUT (16 entries; E2M1 -> FP16 is exact) + block scales in the accumulator domain (E8M0 = power-of-two FP16 multiply, exact while in-range; E4M3 = the FP8 rebias already landed in stages 2-3), riding the W4A16 staged/regdequant kernel family and the plan/0004 block-scale machinery - no upstream dependency, all sm75-sanctioned PTX. Triton codegen gate: upstream's MXFP4 execution (gpt-oss triton_kernels matmul_ogs, and tl.dot_scaled emulation generally) requires triton >= 3.4 with BF16 upcast - structurally unavailable on sm75 twice over (no BF16; and Triton 3.3+ dropped pre-Ampere from the MMA path: PR #5066 'Deprecate MMAv1; fallback to FMA for computeCapability < 80' merged 2024-11-05, shipped 3.3.0, so dot_scaled emulation on sm75 lowers to FMA-only codegen; Triton 3.3.0 additionally crashed on cuda:75 with the f16->f16 LLVM error, #6698, fixed by #7585 2025-07-22; the lane pin triton <= 3.2 keeps MMAv2 m16n8k8 tensor cores but conflicts with triton_kernels >= 3.4). Consequence: tl.dot_scaled is NOT the emulation vehicle for this host - the fork's CUDA nibble path is, and the Triton FMA floor only matters as the reason the 'obvious portable' route is a trap. Attention-backend candidate matrix where it gates this item (gpt-oss serving): upstream vLLM floors FlashInfer at SM80 and has no working sm75 engine (sibling record turing-engine-upstream-drift); the fork's retained Turing engine runs the TRITON_ATTN leg (fp16), which is the only leg an MXFP4-recast gpt-oss can ride; gpt-oss's alternating sliding-window(128)+global attention with sinks is not validated on that leg [uncertain]. Measured numbers on this rig for the shared substrate: incumbent sm75 Marlin 51-57 TFLOP/s at M512, FP16 tensor ceiling 101.7 TFLOP/s at locked 1455 MHz, DRAM 535 GB/s; at M=1 an MXFP4/NVFP4-resident model decodes at half the bytes of W8A16 FP8 and the same bytes-per-weight as the fork's INT4 path, so decode is bandwidth-bound and unaffected by FP4-ness; the fp16-accumulator risk of the upstream Turing Marlin port (adopted because the author measured MMA throughput halving with FP32 accum on Turing - contradicted by this host's microbench, see sibling record) applies to any reuse of upstream Marlin FP4 kernels and must be oracle-gated at large K.

Rebase consequence: the fork's adapters consume checkpoint bits, not upstream kernels - the load-bearing upstream facts are the scale-layout constants (gpt-oss MXFP4 packing, compressed-tensors mxfp4-pack-quantized, ModelOpt NVFP4 double-block E4M3 + global FP32) and the #34577 lesson (E4M3 scale dynamic range vs the rebias), all of which are stable; no upstream release dropped FP4-on-sm75 because none ever shipped a verified working MXFP4-on-sm75 path to drop.

effort_value.effort_estimate: Two adapter rows plus shared LUT machinery - a medium campaign, not a kernel-ladder rewrite, because stages 2-5 (FP8 rebias/LUT, recast loader, byte-dequant strategy rows, format axis in selection) are prerequisites already scoped and the nibble path is narrower than the FP8 byte path (4 bits, not 8). Stage 8 (MXFP4): checkpoint adapter for compressed-tensors mxfp4-pack-quantized + the gpt-oss native packing (E2M1 x2 per byte, E8M0 per 32, swizzled scale tiles), 16-entry nibble LUT into the staged/regdequant family, E8M0 scale as power-of-two FP16 multiply in the accumulator-domain machinery (plan/0004), float64 oracle (exact: all E2M1 x E8M0 products representable), recast path = LUT at load. Stage 9 (NVFP4): same LUT, E4M3 per-16 scales dequantized by the already-landed FP8 rebias, per-tensor FP32 global scale folded at load (exact), adapter for ModelOpt hf_quant_config (NVFP4/W4A16_NVFP4) + compressed-tensors detection (_is_nvfp4_format). Rough size: 1-2 sessions per adapter for adapter+oracle, 2-4 more for ladder runs of the nibble-dequant rows reusing the existing W4A16 dispatch harness; no new harness, no new PTX. The gpt-oss end-to-end (MXFP4 recast generate on the retained Turing engine) adds engine-integration time, dominated by the attention-leg validation, not the format.
effort_value.unlocks: The incoming-format contract for the two formats the 2026 checkpoint wave actually ships: gpt-oss-20b (MXFP4-native, ~14 GB as FP4 weights - single-card on a 24 GB TU102 at W4A16 residency, both cards for throughput) and the NVFP4 family - nvidia/Qwen3-14B-NVFP4, nvidia/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-NVFP4 (~42.7 GB, TP2-partial on 48 GB aggregate [uncertain fit with KV]), nm-testing/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-NVFP4A16, and the community Qwen3.x-27B NVFP4A16 checkpoints (kkuspa/huginnfork, ~15 GB weights, advertised 'Ampere+ ~32 GB, no Blackwell required') which sit exactly on the operator's Qwen3-class ~27B target from plan/0005. Also completes the format axis (stage 5) for the FP4 row, halves W4A16 memory again versus the FP8 stage (0.5 byte/weight + scales), keeps the stored-value contract llama.cpp cannot offer for NVFP4 (GGUF conversion re-quantizes; the adapter executes the exact stored E2M1 x scale products), and closes the #23203/#33461 class of upstream refusals: nothing upstream will ever run gpt-oss MXFP4 natively on sm75 (BF16-only activation dtype in code), so the fork becomes the only vLLM-lineage stack that does.
effort_value.dependency_order: Internal, first: stages 1-3 of plan/0005 (checkpoint adapter IR, recast path, byte-dequant strategy rows - the FP8 E4M3 rebias/LUT that stage 9's scale conversion reuses verbatim) and stage 5 (format axis in the dispatch table, so an adapter is selectable); the W4A16 nibble machinery from plans/0002-0004 (staged/regdequant kernel family, winner gates) supplies the execution rows - already landed. Stage 8 (MXFP4) and stage 9 (NVFP4) can proceed in parallel once stages 1-3 exist; they share the nibble LUT, which should be built once (stage 8 lands it, stage 9 reuses). The gpt-oss end-to-end demo additionally depends on the engine row (stage 11 / the retained Turing engine on the TRITON_ATTN leg) - not on any new format work but on that row staying healthy. External prerequisites: none - checkpoints are public on HF (openai/gpt-oss-20b, nvidia/Qwen3-14B-NVFP4, nm-testing/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct-MXFP4 as the dense smoke model), the OCP spec defines the constants, and the reference dequant exists in transformers (CC 7.5) for oracle cross-checking. Not gating but informative: upstream Marlin FP4 kernels exist as a comparison baseline only (their sm75 FP4 correctness is the open question, not a dependency).
effort_value.risk_notes: Numerics: (1) E8M0 range (2^-127..2^127) exceeds FP16 (min normal 2^-14) - a raw power-of-two FP16 multiply silently flushes extreme block scales to zero/subnormal; the adapter must fold out-of-range exponents into the per-tensor prescale at load and report, never truncate (the same never-silent rule as the bf16->fp16 stage-10 overflow check). (2) E4M3 scale dynamic range vs the rebias is exactly the #34577 bug class - upstream multiplied scales by 2^7 assuming MSB=1 and models with global_scale=1 (GLM-4.7-Flash-NVFP4) underflowed to ~2^-112; the fork's rebias is exact (no assumption), but the oracle must include small-scale and asymmetric-scale blocks so a widening error cannot pass clean. (3) FP16 accumulation depth: NVFP4's per-16 blocks mean scale multiplies happen 2x as often as MXFP4's per-32; if any reused kernel accumulates in FP16 (the upstream Turing Marlin choice), large-K tensors need explicit oracle coverage at K=11008-class depth. (4) Packing ambiguity: E2M1 pairs per byte and the swizzled scale tile layouts differ between gpt-oss packing and compressed-tensors mxfp4-pack-quantized - a nibble-order or tile-offset error produces plausible-looking garbage (the #33461 signature), so the oracle must check per-block, not just per-tensor, error. Silent fallbacks: vLLM's 'default to dequantizing the model' warning path (CC<9.0) silently converts to BF16 at 4x memory - a sm75 load must fail loudly rather than ride it; upstream --linear-backend=marlin for NVFP4 on sm75 post-#34577 is unverified (#33461 undiagnosed) and must not be treated as a reference without local oracle diffing. Upstream drift: low - the checkpoint formats and scale layouts are spec/contract-stable; exposure is limited to future packing variants and the Marlin alignment floor (#38022 class, K=N=2880 on gpt-oss) which the fork's own dispatch must handle independently.
effort_value.determinism_class: Bitwise class per configuration for the fork's path: E2M1 LUT and both scale conversions (E8M0 power-of-two multiply, E4M3 rebias) are exact functions of the stored bits, so the dequant reference is a float64 oracle with zero representation slack - an exact-diff gate, like the FP8 stage. The GEMM itself: fixed tile traversal and k-order, no atomics in the non-split path - bit-exact run-to-run at fixed shape/config; split-K/global-reduce rows (if admitted from the existing family for small-M) introduce the known statistical class (atomicAdd ordering) and must be gated on the fixed-order epilogue or bounded by the adversarial oracle set, exactly as the W4A16 record requires. Restart-to-restart: scale-prescale folding happens at load (deterministic function of the checkpoint), workspace zeroing is the caller contract, CUDA-graph capture must express any per-replay recompute (existing replay-validation machinery covers it). The float64-oracle + median-of-N discipline needs: per-block (not per-tensor) oracle cases, small-scale/E4M3-range adversarial cases (the #34577 class), asymmetric nibble pairs (interleave class), and K-depth accumulation cases if any FP16-accum row is admitted. Upstream comparison runs (Marlin on sm75) are statistical-class evidence only and never a substitute for the oracle.

decision.priority_signal: For: the checkpoint wave is here and the operator's target class is directly named - gpt-oss ships MXFP4-native and the NVFP4A16 27B-class community checkpoints advertise exactly the 'no Blackwell required' niche this fork exists for; upstream has now twice refused the sm75 door (#23203 closed not planned; #33461 closed stale) and the MXFP4 path is structurally closed (BF16-only activations in code), so the window is not closing - it is permanently open for the fork to own; effort is low relative to every other plan/0005 row (reuses FP8 rebias + nibble machinery + format axis); and the stored-value contract differentiates against llama.cpp for NVFP4 (re-quantized there, exact here). Against: llama.cpp already runs gpt-oss MXFP4 on Turing since 2025-08, so the 'test before llama.cpp backports' urgency is gone for MXFP4 and the remaining edge is exactness plus vLLM-engine serving; the recast path (transformers-style fp16 dequant) already proves the bits work, so the emulate path's value is purely the 4x footprint and decode bytes, which the INT4 W4A16 path also delivers for models available in GPTQ/AWQ; and the gpt-oss end-to-end is gated on the engine row's health, which is the scarcer resource. Net: schedule soon after the FP8 stages (small marginal cost, real model-class unlock), but it does not displace the engine row.
decision.recommended_probe: Gate-0, oracle-first, no new kernels, three steps. (1) Bit-exactness probe (one session): pull nm-testing/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct-MXFP4 and nvidia/Qwen3-14B-NVFP4, write the 16-entry E2M1 LUT + E8M0/E4M3 scale dequant in plain torch, and diff against the float64 oracle per block (including the E8M0-exceeds-FP16 range cases and the global_scale=1 E4M3 case from #34577) - this settles the adapter contract before any kernel work. (2) Recast viability probe (one session): load Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct-MXFP4 through the recast path (LUT at load -> fp16) on TU102 and generate with the retained engine, output sanity-checked - proves the format bits + engine coexist on sm75 and gives the same-day 'test the model today' capability the plan promises. (3) Upstream-truth probe (one session, settles #33461 for this host): run current upstream vLLM on the RTX 6000 with nvidia/Qwen3-14B-NVFP4, --linear-backend marlin, twice - once default BF16 and once --dtype float16 - diff outputs against the oracle-recast generation; if BF16 is garbage and FP16 is clean, the #34577 widening bug fully explains #33461 and upstream Marlin becomes a usable comparison baseline on sm75; if FP16 is also wrong, the Turing FP4 Marlin path has an unresolved defect and the fork's own kernels are the only route (either way the finding is decision-grade). Timing only after oracles pass; no tl.dot_scaled experiments - the Triton 3.3 FMA floor makes that route a documented trap on sm75.
